use_case: Build long-running, stateful LLM agents and agentic workflows.
Model agent control flow as explicit graphs with nodes, edges, state, and conditional routing.
Support human-in-the-loop review, streaming, persistence, and durable execution for production AI systems.
pros: Strong fit for LLM/agent orchestration, especially when workflows need state, branching, memory, and human checkpoints.
Low-level graph model gives developers precise control over agent behavior instead of forcing a fixed agent architecture.
Can be used standalone, while also integrating naturally with LangChain and LangSmith for models, tools, tracing, debugging, and evaluation.
Durable execution and persistence help long-running agents recover from interruptions.
cons: More specialized for AI agents than general business process or data pipeline orchestration.
Lower-level control means teams must design graph structure, state schema, routing, and operational patterns themselves.
Production observability and evaluation are strongest when paired with LangSmith, which may add platform dependency.
Less suitable when the primary need is non-AI distributed transaction orchestration or large-scale data pipeline scheduling.
